title: Bounded verifier-feedback construction comparison
claim_question: Does bounded verifier feedback improve construction outcomes over deterministic, one-shot, and budget-matched controls on a frozen normal-evidence cohort?

can_test: construction acceptance and explicit terminal outcomes
natural feedback activation and conditional repair success
repeat stability of stochastic construction arms
cannot_test: Agentic benefit from synthetic fault injection
claim_boundary.zero_feedback_conclusion: Bounded feedback capability is implemented, but feedback benefit is not demonstrated.

natural.selection: all eligible relations in the frozen V2 construction cohort; no outcome-driven subset
natural.inputs: normal-only frozen relation evidence and numeric references

fault_injection_stress.selection: precommitted coverage fixtures for terminal and controller paths
fault_injection_stress.purpose: contract, taxonomy, controller, and custody verification only

mapping_invariants: unsupported variable in a parsed proposal maps to VERIFIER_REJECTION, not UNSUPPORTED_EVIDENCE
UNSUPPORTED_EVIDENCE is a deterministic pre-construction evidence eligibility outcome
successful transport with absent or incomplete structured payload maps to EMPTY_RESPONSE
non-empty invalid JSON or strict-schema failure maps to PARSE_FAILURE
repairable verifier outcomes at the fixed budget limit map to BUDGET_EXHAUSTION
retrieval identity or integrity failure maps to RETRIEVAL_FAILURE
custody, persistence, invariant, or unexpected local failure maps to SYSTEM_ERROR

T0.repeat_policy: one deterministic run plus synthetic self-consistency tests

T1-B.construction: three independent initial proposals under the T2-matched maximum budget
T1-B.selection: lowest admissible call index after all three calls

T2.retrieval_scope: targeted re-presentation of evidence already in the initial corpus

privacy.credential_source: approved environment or secret store at transport layer only
privacy.public_outputs: sanitized counts, hashes, statuses, and aggregate metrics only

primary_metrics.denominator: all scheduled relation-arm-repeat records without run-level custody abort

primary_metrics.numerator: T2 records accepted after revise or retrieve
primary_metrics.denominator: T2 records with at least one revise or retrieve action

primary_metrics.numerator: semantic no-rule records confirmed by the deterministic evidence/no-rule validator

repeat_stability_metrics: pairwise Jaccard of accepted relation identities
dispersion of first-call and eventual acceptance
dispersion of feedback activation and repair success
dispersion of calls, tokens, and latency
implementation_plan: add the closed V2 terminal enum and relation-arm-repeat terminal artifact
build lossless adapters from parser, provider ledger, verifier, controller, retrieval, and system receipts
preserve all T1-B draw-level outcomes before deterministic selection
materialize retrieval and system failures without converting them to no_rule
freeze natural and synthetic-stress schedules in separate namespaces
add complete-schedule, privacy, self-hash, mutation, and terminal-class negative tests
freeze provider-visible projection, exact model, maximum call and token budgets before DG-03
obtain independent QA PASS before any provider contact
required_test_cases: one positive and multiple mismatch tests for every terminal class
provider refusal, empty response, and parse failure remain distinct
repairable verifier outcomes at call three are BUDGET_EXHAUSTION
wrong or repeated retrieval is RETRIEVAL_FAILURE
T1-B always uses three calls and retains draw causes
T1-B and T2 maximum generation budget is equal
no raw labels, rows, test data, local paths, credentials, or other arm results enter provider view
network and credential access remain zero while DG-03 is pending
natural and stress artifacts cannot be combined
partial, stale, wrong-authority, and rehashed mutations fail closed
decision_gate_requirements: maximum calls by arm and in total
maximum estimated input, output, and total tokens
